<description>
ProcessBlock() stamps m_last_block_time only after ProcessNewBlock() returns, so getblockcount can show the new height, with nothing in flight, before the stamp is taken. A bumpmocktime in that gap stamps the block with the bumped time, and the final bump then leaves the ping timeout exactly at its boundary, where it never fires. Sync with a ping after the last block, so the node has finished processing it before the clock moves.

The race has been present since the test was added in #36080.

Faling job:
https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/40589303246/job/122489039018
</description>

diff --git a/test/functional/p2p_ping_ibd.py b/test/functional/p2p_ping_ibd.py
index 21aa5fbc23..d145ffe570 100755
--- a/test/functional/p2p_ping_ibd.py
+++ b/test/functional/p2p_ping_ibd.py
@@ -196,6 +196,9 @@ class PingIBDTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
             peer.serve_next_block()
         self.wait_until(lambda: node.getblockcount() == start_height + NUM_DOWNLOAD_BLOCKS)
         assert_equal(node.getpeerinfo()[0]["inflight"], [])
+        # The node stamps the last block time only after the block is connected, so wait until it
+        # handled a message sent after the block before moving the clock.
+        peer.sync_with_ping()
 
         self.log.info("Check that the peer still gets a grace period to answer the ping")
         node.bumpmocktime(POST_BLOCK_PONG_GRACE // 2)
